text: The next morning, Taeo and Nib reached Ryu Survey's West practice yard with twenty-two days until the review. A maze of plywood screens filled the lot. One of the vans had a seizure strip across its door.
Haein, Minho's sister, was repairing a radio. Seeing Taeo's folder, she mistook him for someone from Bluebird. Taeo quickly explained that Chae had sent them.
Minho came over and ordered Nib to talk. Nib answered, 'You first.' Haein immediately looked delighted. Minho accepted the correction and introduced himself properly.
Ryu Survey mapped gates before the clear teams entered. Cheaply, Haein added. Nib introduced himself as a scout. Minho knew Chae wanted him to vouch for Nib, but he needed to see what Nib could do.
The test involved taking a loaded trolley through the maze. Nib would scout ahead, and Taeo would push. The screens blocked Taeo's view, so he had to follow Nib's directions without guessing.
Haein handed them radios and explained the button: hold it to speak, release it to listen. Nib called his a small shouting brick. Taeo was more concerned about the spare screw left on the bench.
Nib went down the left passage and began describing the gap at its end. Taeo pressed his own talk button before Nib finished. Eager to get moving, he announced that he was coming.
The trolley jammed in the narrow gap. From the other side, Nib used his radio to explain the problem. He had said he went left. He hadn't said the cart would fit.
Taeo realised he had cut Nib off. Above them, Minho blamed him for a new grey hair, then gave the useful instruction: take the cart back and let Nib finish looking.
On the second attempt, Taeo kept his thumb off the button and waited. Nib measured the gap, checked the longer route, and reported that the right passage would fit the cart all the way through.
This time, Taeo reached the exit with the load intact. Nib complained that he had taken long enough. Minho agreed it had been slower, but Taeo had finally stopped guessing.
Minho offered the next job directly to Nib: walk the new course before his crew the following morning. One hour, twenty thousand won in cash. Nib asked Taeo what that amount bought.
Taeo translated it into two of his lunches. Nib accepted. Minho also promised a receipt for the review, giving Nib proof of work he had chosen himself.
Taeo asked whether he could work too. Minho told him he needed more practice before guiding anyone. He could watch. As Minho showed Nib around, Taeo was left standing beside the trolley.
Nib noticed Taeo was annoyed and said he hadn't asked Minho to leave him out. Taeo knew that. He had wanted to be good at guiding Nib.
Nib's advice was to let him finish a sentence. Taeo couldn't help laughing. Nib was right, which was precisely what made it annoying.

The following morning, Nib walked the reset course alone. He found cord lying across the exit and wrapped around a screen's foot. Minho acknowledged the warning. Taeo watched anxiously from a stack of pallets.
Haein said Taeo looked like a dog waiting at a door. He apologised. At the end of the hour, Minho counted two notes into Nib's hands. Both belonged to him.

For the receipt, Minho asked for a full name. Nib's full name was simply Nib. He tucked the money and paper into his pouch. Offered the same job next week, he said he would tell Minho whether he wanted it.
At a noodle shop, Nib asked the price of a bowl. The server answered Taeo: seven thousand won. Taeo automatically reached for his wallet and offered to pay for Nib.
Nib pushed Taeo's wallet hand back down. 'I'm buying mine.' He then solemnly offered both his notes. The server explained that one ten thousand won note was enough.
With his change and untouched second note, Nib had thirteen thousand won left. He settled over his bowl and tasted the broth, ears relaxing. Taeo watched him enjoy the meal he had paid for himself.
Grandma messaged to ask about Sunday. Haru kept asking when Taeo would come and wanted spicy seaweed snacks. Taeo told Nib that home was three hours away by bus.
Nib asked whether he could come. Nobody had ever asked to come home with Taeo before. Caught off guard and suddenly warm, Taeo said he would ask Grandma.

Grandma's first concern was whether Taeo was eating. He assured her he was, then explained that he had awakened that week and summoned a goblin. Her startled response was loud enough to flatten Nib's ears.
She immediately asked whether Taeo was going into gates. He said no. He had been to the assessment office. His companion's name was Nib, he talked, and he had asked to visit.
Grandma considered the fish in her kitchen and asked, 'Does he eat fish?' Taeo checked with Nib, then confirmed that he did. That settled it. Grandma ordered both of them to come on Sunday at noon.
After Grandma hung up, Nib pointed out that Taeo's noodles were getting cold. They finished lunch, and Nib reached the crossing while Taeo was still struggling into his shoes.
Taeo called for him to wait. Nib observed that shoes were slow. A bus blocked Taeo's view along the road. Beyond its front bumper, Nib's ear suddenly turned toward something approaching.
An amber pulse struck Taeo's palm before he could see the danger. He snapped upright and shouted Nib's name. A delivery scooter shot out from behind the bus, running the red vehicle signal.
Nib sprang sideways clear of its path. The rider sped away, calling an apology because he was late. Nobody was hit. Nib crouched on the refuge island, breathing hard.
Across the crossing, Taeo's raised hand still trembled with amber light. Nib stared at him. Taeo couldn't have seen past the bus, yet he had felt the danger. 'From there.'
